paragraph: Single-family is the Teaneck market, with 114 sales over six months at a median of $685,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.026, and 68 percent of homes closing above asking in a median of 20 days. That is a seller's market, and multiple offer situations are common on the well-prepared listings. The typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial with two full baths, with capes making up most of the rest. Sales ran from $340,000 to $2,997,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series shows medians still climbing, from $668,000 in February to $726,000 in July, with volume peaking at 34 closings in June. That is the normal spring-into-summer build, so if Teaneck follows the usual arc, expect medians to ease as fall sets in and closings to taper modestly before bottoming in deep winter. Condos and townhouses are a small slice at 9 sales, median $480,000, mostly two-bedroom townhouses, and they moved fast at 16 days. Two-family and three-family sales were only three at a median of $850,000, and co-ops were three more at a median of $171,500, where board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction come with the lower price, which not every buyer is aware of going in. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse, the rental income of a two-family, or the lower entry price of a co-op.
